Detailed Description

Encapsulates the symbol table and provides methods to add new
symbols and look up existing symbols. Nested scopes are supported
and, by default, the add and lookup methods take any ancestor
symbol tables into consideration (ones attached to nodes that are
ancestors of the node that this symbol table is attached to). If the
default visibility is not specified then it defaults to
Symbol.Visbility.PUBLIC.

:param node: reference to the Schedule or Container to which this
    symbol table belongs.
:type node: Optional[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Schedule` |
                     :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Container`]
:param default_visibility: optional default visibility value for this
    symbol table, if not provided it defaults to PUBLIC visibility.
:type default_visibillity: Optional[
    :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol.Visibility`]

:raises TypeError: if node argument is not a Schedule or a Container.

1975 def __eq__(self, other):
1976 '''
1977 Checks whether two SymbolTables are equal.
1978
1979 # TODO 1698: Improve. Currently it uses a quick implementation
1980 # that only checks that the view() lines of each symbol_table
1981 # are exactly the same.
1982 # The current implementation does not check tags, order
1983 # of arguments or visibilities.
1984
1985 :param object other: the object to check equality to.
1986
1987 :returns: whether other is equal to self.
1988 :rtype: bool
1989 '''
1990 # pylint: disable=unidiomatic-typecheck
1991 if type(self) is not type(other):
1992 return False
1993 this_lines = self.view().split('\n')
1994 other_lines = other.view().split('\n')
1995 for line in other_lines:
1996 if line not in this_lines:
1997 return False
1998 this_lines.remove(line)
1999 return len(this_lines) == 0

1902 header = "Symbol Table"
1903 if self.node:
1904 header += f" of {self.node.coloured_name(False)}"

1906 header += f" '{self.node.name}'"

1909

1912 for symbol in self._symbols.values()})
1913 symbol_types.sort(key=lambda t: t.__name__)
1914 for symbol_type in symbol_types:
1915 header += symbol_type.__name__ + ":\n"
1916 # _symbols is an OrderDict so these are alpha-sorted.

1918 # pylint: disable=unidiomatic-typecheck
1919 if type(symbol) is symbol_type:
1920 header += f" {symbol}\n"

689 def _add_container_symbols_from_table(self, other_table):
690 '''
691 Takes container symbols from the supplied symbol table and adds them to
692 this table. All references to each container symbol are also updated.
693 (This is a preliminary step to adding all symbols from other_table to
694 this table.)
695
696 :param other_table: the symbol table from which to take container
697 symbols.
698 :type other_table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`
699
700 '''
701 for csym in other_table.containersymbols:
702 if csym.name in self:
703 # We have a clash with another symbol in this table.
704 self_csym = self.lookup(csym.name)
705 if not isinstance(self_csym, ContainerSymbol):
706 # The symbol in *this* table is not a Container so we
707 # may be able to rename it.
708 self.rename_symbol(
709 self_csym,
710 self.next_available_name(
711 csym.name, other_table=other_table))
712 # We can then add an import from the Container.
713 self.add(csym)
714 else:
715 # The symbol in *this* table is also a ContainerSymbol so
716 # must refer to the same Container. If there is a wildcard
717 # import from this Container then we'll need that in this
718 # Table too.
719 if csym.wildcard_import:
720 self_csym.wildcard_import = True
721 else:
722 self.add(csym)
723 # We must update all references to this ContainerSymbol
724 # so that they point to the one in this table instead.
725 imported_syms = other_table.symbols_imported_from(csym)
726 for isym in imported_syms:
727 if isym.name in self:
728 # We have a potential clash with a symbol imported
729 # into the other table.
730 other_sym = self.lookup(isym.name)
731 if not other_sym.is_import:
732 # The calling merge() method has already checked that
733 # we don't have a clash between symbols of the same
734 # name imported from different containers. We don't
735 # support renaming an imported symbol but the
736 # symbol in this table can be renamed so we do that.
737 self.rename_symbol(
738 other_sym,
739 self.next_available_name(
740 other_sym.name, other_table=other_table))
741 isym.interface = ImportInterface(
742 self.lookup(csym.name),
743 orig_name=isym.interface.orig_name)

778 def _handle_symbol_clash(self, old_sym, other_table):
779 '''
780 Adds the supplied Symbol to the current table in the presence
781 of a name clash. `check_for_clashes` MUST have been called
782 prior to this method in order to check for any unresolvable cases.
783
784 :param old_sym: the Symbol to be added to self.
785 :type old_sym: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
786 :param other_table: the other table containing the symbol that we are
787 trying to add to self.
788 :type other_table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`
789
790 :raises InternalError: if the supplied symbol is imported from a
791 Container that is not represented in this table.
792
793 '''
794 if old_sym.is_import:
795 # This symbol is imported from a Container so should
796 # already have been updated so as to be imported from the
797 # corresponding container in this table.
798 self_csym = self.lookup(old_sym.interface.container_symbol.name)
799 if old_sym.interface.container_symbol is self_csym:
800 return
801 raise InternalError(
802 f"Symbol '{old_sym.name}' imported from '{self_csym.name}' "
803 f"has not been updated to refer to the corresponding "
804 f"container in the current table.")
805
806 self_sym = self.lookup(old_sym.name)
807 if old_sym.is_unresolved and self_sym.is_unresolved:
808 # The clashing symbols are both unresolved so we ASSUME that
809 # check_for_clashes has previously determined that they must
810 # refer to the same thing and we don't have to do anything.
811 return
812
813 # A Symbol with the same name already exists so we attempt to rename
814 # first the one that we are adding and failing that, the existing
815 # symbol in this table.
816 new_name = self.next_available_name(
817 old_sym.name, other_table=other_table)
818 try:
819 other_table.rename_symbol(old_sym, new_name)
820 self.add(old_sym)
821 except SymbolError:
822 self.rename_symbol(self_sym, new_name)
823 self.add(old_sym)
824

1096 '''
1097 Checks whether the supplied RoutineSymbol can be removed from this
1098 table.

1104 :type symbol: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.RoutineSymbol`
1105

1111 try:

1113 # outer scope then we can safely delete its entry in this table
1114 # as all references to it will remain valid.

553 def add(self, new_symbol, tag=None):
554 '''Add a new symbol to the symbol table if the symbol name is not
555 already in use.
556
557 :param new_symbol: the symbol to add to the symbol table.
558 :type new_symbol: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
559 :param str tag: a tag identifier for the new symbol, by default no \
560 tag is given.
561
562 :raises InternalError: if the new_symbol argument is not a \
563 symbol.
564 :raises KeyError: if the symbol name is already in use.
565 :raises KeyError: if a tag is supplied and it is already in \
566 use.
567
568 '''
569 if not isinstance(new_symbol, Symbol):
570 raise InternalError(f"Symbol '{new_symbol}' is not a symbol, but "
571 f"'{type(new_symbol).__name__}'.'")
572
573 key = self._normalize(new_symbol.name)
574 if key in self._symbols:
575 raise KeyError(f"Symbol table already contains a symbol with "
576 f"name '{new_symbol.name}'.")
577 if tag:
578 if tag in self.get_tags():
579 raise KeyError(
580 f"This symbol table, or an outer scope ancestor symbol "
581 f"table, already contains the tag '{tag}' for the symbol"
582 f" '{self.lookup_with_tag(tag).name}', so it can not be "
583 f"associated with symbol '{new_symbol.name}'.")
584 self._tags[tag] = new_symbol
585
586 self._symbols[key] = new_symbol

588 def check_for_clashes(self, other_table, symbols_to_skip=()):
589 '''
590 Checks the symbols in the supplied table against those in
591 this table. If there is a name clash that cannot be resolved by
592 renaming then a SymbolError is raised. Any symbols appearing
593 in `symbols_to_skip` are excluded from the checks.
594
595 :param other_table: the table for which to check for clashes.
596 :type other_table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`
597 :param symbols_to_skip: an optional list of symbols to exclude from
598 the check.
599 :type symbols_to_skip: Iterable[
600 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`]
601
602 :raises TypeError: if symbols_to_skip is supplied but is not an
603 instance of Iterable.
604 :raises SymbolError: if there would be an unresolvable name clash
605 when importing symbols from `other_table` into this table.
606
607 '''
608 # pylint: disable-next=import-outside-toplevel
609 from psyclone.psyir.nodes import IntrinsicCall
610
611 if not isinstance(symbols_to_skip, Iterable):
612 raise TypeError(
613 f"check_for_clashes: 'symbols_to_skip' must be an instance of "
614 f"Iterable but got '{type(symbols_to_skip).__name__}'")
615
616 # Check whether there are any wildcard imports common to both tables.
617 self_imports = self.wildcard_imports()
618 other_imports = other_table.wildcard_imports()
619 shared_wildcard_imports = self_imports & other_imports
620 # Any wildcard imports that appear in one table but not in the other.
621 unique_wildcard_imports = self_imports ^ other_imports
622
623 for other_sym in other_table.symbols:
624 if other_sym.name not in self or other_sym in symbols_to_skip:
625 continue
626 # We have a name clash.
627 this_sym = self.lookup(other_sym.name)
628
629 # If they are both ContainerSymbols then that's OK as they refer to
630 # the same Container.
631 if (isinstance(this_sym, ContainerSymbol) and
632 isinstance(other_sym, ContainerSymbol)):
633 continue
634
635 # If they are both IntrinsicSymbol then that's fine.
636 if (isinstance(this_sym, IntrinsicSymbol) and
637 isinstance(other_sym, IntrinsicSymbol)):
638 continue
639
640 if other_sym.is_import and this_sym.is_import:
641 # Both symbols are imported. That's fine as long as they have
642 # the same import interface (are imported from the same
643 # Container and refer to the same Symbol in that Container).
644 if this_sym.interface != other_sym.interface:
645 raise SymbolError(
646 f"This table has an import of '{this_sym.name}' via "
647 f"interface '{this_sym.interface}' but the supplied "
648 f"table imports it via '{other_sym.interface}'.")
649 continue
650
651 if other_sym.is_unresolved and this_sym.is_unresolved:
652 # Both Symbols are unresolved.
653 if shared_wildcard_imports and not unique_wildcard_imports:
654 # The tables have one or more wildcard imports in common
655 # and no wildcard imports unique to one table. Therefore
656 # the two symbols represent the same memory location.
657 continue
658 if not (self_imports or other_imports):
659 # Neither table has any wildcard imports.
660 try:
661 # An unresolved symbol representing an intrinisc is OK
662 _ = IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic[this_sym.name.upper()]
663 # Take this opportunity to specialise the symbol(s).
664 if not isinstance(this_sym, IntrinsicSymbol):
665 this_sym.specialise(IntrinsicSymbol)
666 if not isinstance(other_sym, IntrinsicSymbol):
667 other_sym.specialise(IntrinsicSymbol)
668 continue
669 except KeyError:
670 pass
671 # We can't rename a symbol if we don't know its origin.
672 raise SymbolError(
673 f"A symbol named '{this_sym.name}' is present but "
674 f"unresolved in one or both tables.")
675
676 # Can either of them be renamed?
677 try:
678 self.rename_symbol(this_sym, "", dry_run=True)
679 except SymbolError as err1:
680 try:
681 other_table.rename_symbol(other_sym, "", dry_run=True)
682 except SymbolError as err2:
683 # pylint: disable=raise-missing-from
684 raise SymbolError(
685 f"There is a name clash for symbol '{this_sym.name}' "
686 f"that cannot be resolved by renaming "
687 f"one of the instances because:\n- {err1}\n- {err2}")
688

1501 def copy_external_import(self, imported_var, tag=None):
1502 '''
1503 Copy the given imported variable (and its referenced ContainerSymbol if
1504 needed) into the SymbolTable.
1505
1506 :param imported_var: the variable to be copied in.
1507 :type imported_var: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`
1508 :param str tag: a tag identifier for the new copy, by default no tag \
1509 is given.
1510
1511 :raises TypeError: if the given variable is not an imported variable.
1512 :raises KeyError: if the given variable name already exists in the \
1513 symbol table.
1514
1515 '''
1516 if not isinstance(imported_var, DataSymbol):
1517 raise TypeError(
1518 f"The imported_var argument of "
1519 f"SymbolTable.copy_external_import method should be a "
1520 f"DataSymbol, but found '{type(imported_var).__name__}'.")
1521
1522 if not imported_var.is_import:
1523 raise TypeError(
1524 f"The imported_var argument of SymbolTable.copy_external_"
1525 f"import method should have an ImportInterface interface, "
1526 f"but found '{type(imported_var.interface).__name__}'.")
1527
1528 external_container_name = imported_var.interface.container_symbol.name
1529
1530 # If the Container is not yet in the SymbolTable we need to
1531 # create one and add it.
1532 if external_container_name not in self:
1533 self.add(ContainerSymbol(external_container_name))
1534 container_ref = self.lookup(external_container_name)
1535
1536 # Copy the variable into the SymbolTable with the appropriate interface
1537 if imported_var.name not in self:
1538 new_symbol = imported_var.copy()
1539 # Update the interface of this new symbol
1540 new_symbol.interface = ImportInterface(container_ref)
1541 self.add(new_symbol, tag)
1542 else:
1543 # If it already exists it must refer to the same Container and have
1544 # the same tag.
1545 local_instance = self.lookup(imported_var.name)
1546 if not (local_instance.is_import and
1547 self._has_same_name(
1548 local_instance.interface.container_symbol,
1549 external_container_name)):
1550 raise KeyError(
1551 f"Couldn't copy '{imported_var}' into the SymbolTable. The"
1552 f" name '{imported_var.name}' is already used by another "
1553 f"symbol.")
1554 if tag:
1555 # If the symbol already exists and a tag is provided
1556 try:
1557 self.lookup_with_tag(tag)
1558 except KeyError:
1559 # If the tag was not used, it will now be attached
1560 # to the symbol.
1561 self._tags[tag] = self.lookup(imported_var.name)
1562
1563 # The tag should not refer to a different symbol
1564 if self.lookup(imported_var.name) != self.lookup_with_tag(tag):
1565 raise KeyError(
1566 f"Couldn't copy '{imported_var}' into the SymbolTable."
1567 f" The tag '{tag}' is already used by another symbol.")

261 def deep_copy(self):
262 '''Create a copy of the symbol table with new instances of the
263 top-level data structures and also new instances of the symbols
264 contained in these data structures. Modifying a symbol attribute
265 will not affect the equivalent named symbol in the original symbol
266 table.
267
268 The only attribute not copied is the _node reference to the scope,
269 since that scope can only have one symbol table associated to it.
270
271 :returns: a deep copy of this symbol table.
272 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`
273
274 '''
275 # pylint: disable=protected-access
276 new_st = type(self)()
277
278 # Make a copy of each symbol in the symbol table
279 for symbol in self.symbols:
280 new_st.add(symbol.copy())
281
282 # Prepare the new argument list
283 new_arguments = []
284 for name in [arg.name for arg in self.argument_list]:
285 new_arguments.append(new_st.lookup(name))
286 new_st.specify_argument_list(new_arguments)
287
288 # Prepare the new tag dict
289 for tag, symbol in self._tags.items():
290 new_st._tags[tag] = new_st.lookup(symbol.name)
291
292 # Update any references to Symbols within Symbols (initial values,
293 # precision etc.)
294 for symbol in new_st.symbols:
295 symbol.replace_symbols_using(new_st)
296
297 # Set the default visibility
298 new_st._default_visibility = self.default_visibility
299
300 return new_st
301

186 def get_symbols(self, scope_limit=None):

1784 symbol table.

1786 imported/unresolved or is a formal routine argument.

1788 CodeBlock in the scope of this table.
1789 :raises SymbolError: if the symbol has a common block interface.

1791 '''
1792 if not isinstance(symbol, Symbol):
1793 raise TypeError(

1821
1822 if symbol.is_commonblock:
1823 raise SymbolError(

1826
1827 if not isinstance(name, str):
1828 raise TypeError(
1829 f"The name argument of rename_symbol() must be a str, but"

1569 def resolve_imports(self, container_symbols=None, symbol_target=None):
1570 ''' Try to resolve deferred and unknown information from imported
1571 symbols in this symbol table by searching for their definitions in
1572 referred external container. A single symbol to resolve can be
1573 specified for a more targeted import.
1574
1575 :param container_symbols: list of container symbols to search in
1576 order to resolve imported symbols. Defaults to all container
1577 symbols in the symbol table.
1578 :type container_symbols: list[
1579 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.ContainerSymbol`]
1580 :param symbol_target: If a symbol is given, this method will just
1581 resolve information for the given symbol. Otherwise it will
1582 resolve all possible symbols information. Defaults to None.
1583 :type symbol_target: Optional[
1584 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`]
1585
1586 :raises SymbolError: if a symbol name clash is found between multiple
1587 imports or an import and a local symbol.
1588 :raises TypeError: if the provided container_symbols is not a list of
1589 ContainerSymbols.
1590 :raises TypeError: if the provided symbol_target is not a Symbol.
1591 :raises KeyError: if a symbol_target has been specified but this has
1592 not been found in any of the searched containers.
1593
1594 '''

1596 if not isinstance(container_symbols, list):
1597 raise TypeError(
1598 f"The resolve_imports container_symbols argument must be a"
1599 f" list but found '{type(container_symbols).__name__}' "
1600 f"instead.")

1602 if not isinstance(item, ContainerSymbol):
1603 raise TypeError(
1604 f"The resolve_imports container_symbols argument list "
1605 f"elements must be ContainerSymbols, but found a "
1606 f"'{type(item).__name__}' instead.")

1609 container_symbols = self.containersymbols
1610

1612 raise TypeError(

1614 f"but found '{type(symbol_target).__name__}' instead.")

1623 # been found in the given include_path or any issue has arisen
1624 # during parsing.

1630 # errors).
1631 continue

868 def swap_symbol_properties(self, symbol1, symbol2):
869 '''Swaps the properties of symbol1 and symbol2 apart from the symbol
870 name. Argument list positions are also updated appropriately.
871
872 :param symbol1: the first symbol.
873 :type symbol1: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
874 :param symbol2: the second symbol.
875 :type symbol2: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
876
877 :raises KeyError: if either of the supplied symbols are not in \
878 the symbol table.
879 :raises TypeError: if the supplied arguments are not symbols, \
880 or the names of the symbols are the same in the SymbolTable \
881 instance.
882
883 '''
884 for symbol in [symbol1, symbol2]:
885 if not isinstance(symbol, Symbol):
886 raise TypeError(f"Arguments should be of type 'Symbol' but "
887 f"found '{type(symbol).__name__}'.")
888 if symbol.name not in self._symbols:
889 raise KeyError(f"Symbol '{symbol.name}' is not in the symbol "
890 f"table.")
891 if self._has_same_name(symbol1.name, symbol2.name):
892 raise ValueError(f"The symbols should have different names, but "
893 f"found '{symbol1.name}' for both.")
894
895 tmp_symbol = symbol1.copy()
896 symbol1.copy_properties(symbol2)
897 symbol2.copy_properties(tmp_symbol)

899 # Update argument list if necessary
900 index1 = None
901 if symbol1 in self._argument_list:
902 index1 = self._argument_list.index(symbol1)
903 index2 = None
904 if symbol2 in self._argument_list:
905 index2 = self._argument_list.index(symbol2)
906 if index1 is not None:
907 self._argument_list[index1] = symbol2
908 if index2 is not None:
909 self._argument_list[index2] = symbol1
